title: “one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved” — who is he?
summary: John 13:23 has “one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved” leaning on Jesus’ bosom, and the same description is used at 19:26, 20:2, 21:7 and 21:20. John 21:24 says “This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things”. The passages give no name for him and do not say whether he is the same man in every place.
text: KJV John 13:23: “one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) John 13:23: ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς [whom Jesus loved]. KJV John 19:26: “the disciple standing by, whom he loved”. KJV John 20:2: “the other disciple, whom Jesus loved”. Greek: τὸν ἄλλον μαθητὴν ὃν ἐφίλει ὁ Ἰησοῦς [the other disciple whom Jesus loved]. KJV John 21:7: “that disciple whom Jesus loved”. KJV John 21:20: “the disciple whom Jesus loved following”. KJV John 21:24: “This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/43/13/, https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/43/13/, https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/43/20/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/43/20/.
reasoning: The description is given without a name each time, and 20:2 calls him “the other disciple” in the same breath as Peter. Different readings are held as possibilities only, among them that he is one of the twelve who were at the supper (13:23), that he is another follower who is not named in the lists, and that the phrase is a way the writer of 21:24 refers to himself. The text does not choose among them, and the answer bears on who stands behind the testimony of 21:24.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the verses quoted. The record does not say who the disciple is, does not say that any one reading is the right one, and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more. The Greek of 19:26, 21:7, 21:20 and 21:24 was not fetched. title: Jesus “wrote on the ground” — what did he write?
summary: John 8:6 says that Jesus “with his finger wrote on the ground”, and 8:8 repeats that he “wrote on the ground”. The passage does not say what he wrote, either time, nor whether it bore on what he said at 8:7.
text: KJV John 8:6: “with his finger wrote on the ground”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) John 8:6: τῷ δακτύλῳ ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν [with the finger was writing on the ground]. KJV John 8:8: “wrote on the ground”. Greek: ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν [was writing on the ground]. KJV John 8:7: “He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her”. KJV John 8:9: “being convicted by their own conscience”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/43/8/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/43/8/.
reasoning: The verb is used twice and the object of the writing is not stated either time. Readings are held as possibilities only: that it was the accusers’ sins, that it was a text, or that it was a gesture without meaning in itself. The text does not choose among them; and the answer bears on what convicted the accusers at 8:9.

title: “a feast of the Jews” — which feast?
summary: John 5:1 says “After this there was a feast of the Jews; and Jesus went up to Jerusalem”, and does not name the feast. John names the passover at 2:13, 6:4 and 11:55 and the feast of tabernacles at 7:2. The passage does not say which feast this is, nor whether it is one of those named elsewhere.
text: KJV John 5:1: “there was a feast of the Jews”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) John 5:1: ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων [feast of the Jews]. KJV John 2:13: “the Jews' passover was at hand”. KJV John 6:4: “the passover, a feast of the Jews, was nigh”. KJV John 7:2: “the Jew's feast of tabernacles was at hand”. KJV John 11:55: “the Jews' passover was nigh at hand”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/43/5/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/43/5/.
reasoning: Elsewhere the gospel names the feast. Here it does not, so the verse leaves open whether this is a passover, which would bear on how many passovers the gospel counts, or another feast. Readings are held as possibilities only, and the text does not choose among them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the verses quoted. The record does not say which feast is meant, does not count the passovers of the gospel, and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more.
